name: Treaty of Adrianople
summary: Ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1828-29, giving Russia the Danube mouth and confirming Greek autonomy.

name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
summary: Ended the Mexican-American War; Mexico ceded roughly half its territory, including California, to the United States.

name: Peace of Milan
summary: Peace between Austria and Sardinia after Novara; Sardinia paid an indemnity and the territorial status quo was restored (some sources date it 9 August).

name: Treaty of Berlin (Prussia-Denmark)
summary: Prussian-Danish peace ending the First Schleswig War; both sides reserved their rights, and the duchies question was settled by the 1852 London Protocol.

name: London Protocol (1852)

judgment.rationale: Historians commonly see the unresolved Schleswig-Holstein question left by the protocol, and the dispute over Denmark's 1863 November Constitution, as the direct cause of the 1864 war.

summary: Great-power protocol upholding the integrity of the Danish monarchy, including Schleswig and Holstein, as a 'European necessity'.

name: Treaty of Paris (1856)

violated.how: Russia repudiated the Black Sea neutralisation clauses in October 1870, and the 1871 London Conference accepted this.

summary: Ended the Crimean War; neutralised the Black Sea (no warships or arsenals) and guaranteed Ottoman integrity.

name: Treaty of Paris (1857)
summary: Ended the Anglo-Persian War; Persia withdrew from Herat and recognised Afghan independence.

name: Treaty of Zurich
summary: Confirmed the Villafranca armistice ending the Second Italian War of Independence; Austria ceded Lombardy (via France) to Sardinia.

name: Treaty of Wad-Ras
summary: Ended the Hispano-Moroccan War; Morocco paid an indemnity and recognised Spanish possession of Ceuta and Melilla with enlarged limits.

name: Treaty of Pinsaqui
summary: Ended the 1863 Ecuadorian-Colombian War after Cuaspud, restoring prior relations without territorial change.

name: Treaty of Vienna (1864)
summary: Ended the Second Schleswig War; Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria.

name: Loizaga-Cotegipe Treaty
summary: Separate Brazil-Paraguay peace after the Paraguayan War, fixing their border.

name: Machain-Irigoyen Treaty
summary: Argentina-Paraguay peace and boundary treaty concluding the Paraguayan War (Chaco Boreal north of the Pilcomayo left to arbitration).

name: Spain-Peru Treaty of Peace and Friendship
summary: Final peace between Spain and Peru after the Chincha Islands War (an indefinite armistice had been signed in Washington in 1871).

name: Chilean-Spanish Treaty of 1883
summary: Signed in Chilean-occupied Lima, formally ending the Chincha Islands War between Chile and Spain.

name: Peace of Prague
summary: Ended the Austro-Prussian War; dissolved the German Confederation and excluded Austria from German affairs.

name: Treaty of Vienna (1866)
summary: Austro-Italian peace ending the Third Italian War of Independence; Venetia passed to Italy.

name: Treaty of London (1867)

violated.how: Germany occupied neutral Luxembourg on 2 August 1914 (and again in 1940).

summary: Settled the Luxembourg crisis: Prussian garrison withdrawn and Luxembourg's perpetual neutrality placed under collective guarantee.

name: Treaty of Frankfurt

judgment.rationale: A standard interpretation holds that the annexation of Alsace-Lorraine created lasting French revanchism and Franco-German enmity that structured the alliance blocs of 1914.

summary: Ended the Franco-Prussian War; France ceded Alsace and most of Lorraine and paid 5 billion francs.

name: Treaty of San Stefano
summary: Preliminary peace ending the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-78, creating a large autonomous Bulgaria; revised at the Congress of Berlin.

name: Treaty of Berlin (1878)

violated.how: Austria-Hungary unilaterally annexed Bosnia-Herzegovina in October 1908, beyond the occupation mandate of Article 25.

judgment.rationale: Historians widely see the Berlin settlement's frustration of Balkan national aspirations (Bulgaria, Serbia, Macedonia) as a root of the Balkan Wars and, through the Bosnian question, of the 1914 crisis.

summary: Great-power revision of San Stefano: Serbia, Montenegro and Romania independent, Bulgaria reduced, Austria-Hungary to occupy Bosnia-Herzegovina.

name: Treaty of Ancon
summary: Chile-Peru peace ending the War of the Pacific; Peru ceded Tarapaca, Tacna and Arica placed under Chilean control pending a plebiscite.

name: Truce Pact of Valparaiso
summary: Indefinite Chile-Bolivia truce ending hostilities in the War of the Pacific; Bolivia's coast (Antofagasta) left under Chilean administration.

name: Treaty of Peace and Friendship (Chile-Bolivia)
summary: Definitive Chile-Bolivia peace; Bolivia recognised the loss of its coastline in exchange for a railway and transit rights.

name: Treaty of Tientsin (1885)
summary: Ended the Sino-French War; China recognised the French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin.

name: Treaty of Shimonoseki

judgment.rationale: Historians commonly argue that the Triple Intervention forcing Japan to return Liaodong, which Russia then leased, fuelled the Russo-Japanese rivalry over Manchuria and Korea that led to the 1904 war.

summary: Ended the First Sino-Japanese War; China recognised Korean independence and ceded Taiwan, the Pescadores and (until the Triple Intervention) Liaodong.

name: Treaty of Constantinople (1897)
summary: Ended the Greco-Turkish War of 1897; Thessaly largely returned to Greece with minor border changes and a heavy indemnity.

name: Treaty of Paris (1898)
summary: Ended the Spanish-American War; Spain relinquished Cuba and ceded Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.

name: Boxer Protocol
summary: Settlement after the Boxer Rebellion imposing a 450 million tael indemnity and foreign legation guards on China.

name: Treaty of Portsmouth

judgment.rationale: One common interpretation traces Japan's 1931 seizure of Manchuria to the railway zone and Kwantung leasehold it gained at Portsmouth, which anchored Japanese expansion there.

summary: US-mediated end of the Russo-Japanese War; Russia ceded southern Sakhalin, the Liaodong lease and the South Manchuria Railway and recognised Japan's paramountcy in Korea.

name: Marblehead Pact
summary: Preliminary peace signed aboard USS Marblehead under US-Mexican auspices ending the 1906 Guatemala-El Salvador/Honduras war.

name: General Treaty of Peace and Amity (Washington 1907)
summary: Treaty of the 1907 Central American Peace Conference ending the 1907 war and creating the Central American Court of Justice.

name: Treaty of Ouchy (First Treaty of Lausanne)
summary: Ended the Italo-Turkish War; Ottoman withdrawal from Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, Italy to hold the Dodecanese temporarily.

name: Treaty of London (1913)

judgment.rationale: Historians agree the treaty left the division of Macedonia among the victors unresolved, prompting Bulgaria's attack on its former allies a month later.

summary: Ended the First Balkan War; Ottoman Empire ceded nearly all European territory west of the Enos-Midia line (MNK = Kingdom of Montenegro).

name: Treaty of Bucharest (1913)

judgment.rationale: A common interpretation is that Bulgarian revisionism after Bucharest drove Sofia into the Central Powers in 1915, while Serbia's enlargement intensified the Austro-Serbian confrontation.

summary: Ended the Second Balkan War; Bulgaria lost most of Macedonia to Serbia and Greece and southern Dobruja to Romania.

name: Treaty of Constantinople (1913)
summary: Ottoman-Bulgarian peace after the Second Balkan War; Edirne returned to the Ottoman Empire.

name: Treaty of London (1839)

violated.how: Germany invaded neutral Belgium on 4 August 1914, prompting Britain's declaration of war.

summary: Recognised Belgian independence and placed its perpetual neutrality under great-power guarantee (the 'scrap of paper').

name: Treaty of London (1915)
summary: Secret pact promising Italy Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman territory in return for entering the war on the Entente side.

name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk

violated.how: The Soviet government annulled the treaty on 13 November 1918 after Germany's armistice in the west.

judgment.rationale: Historians often link the post-1918 borderland wars, including the Polish-Soviet War, to the vacuum left when the German-imposed Brest-Litovsk order in Eastern Europe collapsed.

summary: Soviet Russia's separate peace with the Central Powers, surrendering Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine.

name: Armistice of 11 November 1918
summary: Armistice signed at Compiegne ending fighting on the Western Front.

name: Treaty of Versailles

violated.how: Germany repudiated the military clauses in March 1935 (conscription, Luftwaffe) and remilitarised the Rhineland in March 1936.

judgment.rationale: A long-standing interpretation holds that the treaty's terms fed German revisionism exploited by the Nazis, though many historians stress its weak enforcement as much as its harshness.

summary: Peace with Germany: territorial losses, war-guilt clause, reparations, disarmament and a demilitarised Rhineland (principal signatories listed; US did not ratify).

name: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye

violated.how: The March 1938 Anschluss breached the treaty's ban on Austrian union with Germany.

summary: Peace with Austria: dissolution of the Habsburg Empire recognised and union with Germany (Anschluss) prohibited (principal signatories listed).

name: Treaty of Neuilly-sur-Seine
summary: Peace with Bulgaria: loss of Western Thrace and border districts, reparations and army limits (principal signatories listed).

name: Treaty of Trianon

judgment.rationale: Historians widely regard Trianon revisionism as the main driver of Hungary's alignment with Nazi Germany and its participation in the Second World War.

summary: Peace with Hungary, which lost about two-thirds of its territory; also settled the 1919 Hungarian war with Romania and Czechoslovakia (cow_112).

name: Treaty of Sevres
summary: Partition peace with the Ottoman Empire; never ratified, rejected by the Turkish nationalists and superseded by Lausanne (1923).

name: Treaty of Tartu (Russian-Estonian)

violated.how: The Soviet occupation and annexation of Estonia in June-August 1940 contravened the treaty's recognition of Estonian sovereignty.

summary: Soviet Russia recognised Estonian independence 'in perpetuity', ending the Estonian War of Independence.

name: Treaty of Tartu (Finland-Russia)
summary: Fixed the Finnish-Soviet border (Finland gained Petsamo), ending the Finnish expeditions and hostilities of 1918-20.

name: Latvian-Soviet Peace Treaty

violated.how: The Soviet occupation and annexation of Latvia in 1940 contravened the treaty's recognition of Latvian sovereignty.

summary: Soviet Russia recognised Latvian independence, ending the Latvian War of Independence.

name: Peace of Riga

violated.how: The Soviet invasion of eastern Poland on 17 September 1939 overturned the Riga frontier.

summary: Ended the Polish-Soviet War, fixing Poland's eastern border until 1939 (Soviet Ukraine also signed).

name: Suwalki Agreement

violated.how: Days later General Zeligowski's staged 'mutiny', covertly approved by Pilsudski, seized Vilnius (9 October 1920).

summary: Polish-Lithuanian armistice and demarcation line leaving Vilnius on the Lithuanian side.

name: Treaty of Ankara (1921)
summary: Franco-Turkish (Grand National Assembly) peace ending the Cilicia campaign; France withdrew from Cilicia.

name: Treaty of Lausanne

violated.how: Territorial provisions have largely endured; often cited as the most durable post-WWI settlement.

summary: Replaced Sevres, recognising the Republic of Turkey's borders and ending the Greco-Turkish War and the Allied-Ottoman state of war.

name: Washington Naval Treaty
summary: Capital-ship ratios among the five naval powers; Japan gave notice of withdrawal in December 1934 and the treaty lapsed at the end of 1936.

name: Nine-Power Treaty

violated.how: Japan's seizure of Manchuria from 1931 and the 1937 invasion of China breached the guarantee (the 1937 Brussels Conference was convened under it).

summary: Committed the signatories to respect China's sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity (Open Door).

name: Treaty of Rapallo (1922)
summary: Germany and Soviet Russia renounced war claims and established diplomatic relations.

name: Locarno Treaties (Rhineland Pact)

violated.how: Germany denounced the pact and remilitarised the Rhineland on 7 March 1936.

summary: Guaranteed the Franco-German and Belgian-German borders and the demilitarised Rhineland, with Britain and Italy as guarantors.

name: Italo-Ethiopian Treaty of 1928

violated.how: Italy invaded Ethiopia in October 1935 without recourse to the treaty's dispute procedures.

summary: Twenty-year treaty of friendship with commitment to settle disputes through conciliation/arbitration.

name: Kellogg-Briand Pact

violated.how: Japan's 1931 invasion of Manchuria, Italy's 1935 invasion of Ethiopia and Germany's 1939 aggression contravened the pact; it underpinned the crimes-against-peace charges at Nuremberg.

summary: Renunciation of war as an instrument of national policy (original signatories listed; later near-universal adherence).

name: Khabarovsk Protocol
summary: Restored the status quo ante on the Chinese Eastern Railway, ending the 1929 Sino-Soviet conflict.

name: Soviet-Finnish Non-Aggression Pact

violated.how: The USSR denounced the pact on 28 November 1939 and invaded Finland on 30 November 1939.

summary: Mutual non-aggression treaty, extended in 1934 to 1945.

name: Soviet-Polish Non-Aggression Pact

violated.how: The Soviet Union invaded Poland on 17 September 1939 while the pact was in force.

summary: Mutual non-aggression treaty, extended in 1934 to 1945.

name: Tanggu Truce
summary: Ceasefire creating a demilitarised zone south of the Great Wall, de facto accepting Japan's control of Manchuria.

name: German-Polish Declaration of Non-Aggression

violated.how: Hitler renounced the declaration on 28 April 1939 and invaded Poland on 1 September 1939.

summary: Ten-year German-Polish non-aggression declaration.

name: Treaty of Taif
summary: Ended the Saudi-Yemeni War; Asir, Najran and Jizan remained Saudi.

name: Chaco Peace Protocol (Buenos Aires)
summary: Ceasefire protocol ending fighting in the Chaco War, signed in Buenos Aires.

name: Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Boundaries (Chaco)
summary: Definitive Bolivia-Paraguay peace awarding most of the Chaco Boreal to Paraguay.

name: Anglo-German Naval Agreement

violated.how: Hitler denounced the agreement on 28 April 1939.

summary: Limited the German navy to 35 percent of British surface tonnage.

name: Montreux Convention

violated.how: Remains in force; Turkey invoked it to close the Straits to belligerent warships in 2022.

summary: Restored Turkish control of the Straits and regulated warship passage; still in force.

name: Munich Agreement

violated.how: Germany occupied the rest of Bohemia and Moravia on 15 March 1939.

judgment.rationale: Munich is the standard example of failed appeasement: historians argue it emboldened Hitler and convinced Britain and France that Germany could not be contained without war.

summary: Ceded the Czechoslovak Sudetenland to Germany, with an Anglo-French guarantee of the rump state (Czechoslovakia not a signatory).

name: Lake Khasan ceasefire
summary: Ceasefire negotiated in Moscow after Japan requested peace; fighting stopped on 11 August 1938.

name: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact

violated.how: Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941.

judgment.rationale: Historians generally hold that the pact cleared the way for the German invasion of Poland by removing the threat of a two-front war.

summary: German-Soviet non-aggression treaty with a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of influence.

name: Molotov-Togo ceasefire (Khalkhin Gol)
summary: Soviet-Japanese ceasefire ending the Nomonhan/Khalkhin Gol fighting, effective 16 September 1939.

name: Moscow Peace Treaty

judgment.rationale: Historians widely see Finland's wish to recover the territories lost in 1940 as the main reason it joined the German attack on the USSR in 1941 (Continuation War).

summary: Ended the Winter War; Finland ceded Karelia and other areas.

name: Treaty of Tokyo (1941)
summary: Japanese-mediated peace ending the Franco-Thai War; Vichy France ceded border areas of Laos and Cambodia.

name: Soviet-Japanese Neutrality Pact

violated.how: The USSR denounced the pact in April 1945 and attacked Japan on 9 August 1945 while it was still formally in force.

summary: Five-year mutual neutrality pact.

name: Armistice of Cassibile
summary: Italy's armistice with the Allies, announced 8 September 1943.

name: Moscow Armistice
summary: Ended the Continuation War; Finland restored the 1940 border and ceded Petsamo.

name: German Instrument of Surrender
summary: Unconditional surrender of the German armed forces, signed in Berlin-Karlshorst (after the Reims signing of 7 May).

name: Japanese Instrument of Surrender
summary: Japan's formal surrender aboard USS Missouri.

name: Paris Peace Treaty with Italy (1947)
summary: Italy ceded its colonies, the Dodecanese and border areas and paid reparations; principal Allied signatories listed.

name: Paris Peace Treaty with Romania (1947)
summary: Romania confirmed the loss of Bessarabia and northern Bukovina and regained northern Transylvania; principal Allied signatories listed.

name: Paris Peace Treaty with Hungary (1947)
summary: Hungary returned to its 1938 borders minus three villages ceded to Czechoslovakia; principal Allied signatories listed.

name: Paris Peace Treaty with Bulgaria (1947)
summary: Bulgaria kept southern Dobruja and returned its wartime annexations; principal Allied signatories listed.

name: Paris Peace Treaty with Finland (1947)
summary: Finland confirmed the 1944 armistice borders and paid reparations to the USSR; principal Allied signatories listed.

name: Treaty of San Francisco
summary: Peace with Japan signed by 49 nations (principal signatories listed; USSR attended but did not sign, China not invited).

name: Treaty of Taipei
summary: Peace between Japan and the Republic of China, ending their state of war.

name: Austrian State Treaty

violated.how: Implemented; occupation forces withdrew in 1955.

summary: Ended the four-power occupation and re-established a sovereign Austria, banning Anschluss; followed by Austria's declaration of permanent neutrality.

name: Soviet-Japanese Joint Declaration of 1956
summary: Ended the Soviet-Japanese state of war and restored relations; no peace treaty on the Kuril dispute followed.

name: Treaty of Peace and Friendship between Japan and China
summary: Japan-PRC peace treaty following the 1972 normalisation communique.

name: Treaty of Moscow (1970)

violated.how: Observed until superseded by German reunification arrangements.

summary: West German-Soviet renunciation of force and recognition of existing European borders (Ostpolitik).

name: Treaty of Warsaw (1970)

violated.how: Observed; border confirmed by the 1990 German-Polish Border Treaty.

summary: West Germany recognised the Oder-Neisse line and both renounced the use of force.

name: Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany

violated.how: Implemented; Soviet troops left Germany by 1994.

summary: Two Plus Four Treaty ending four-power rights and serving as the final WWII peace settlement for Germany.

name: Israel-Egypt Armistice Agreement
summary: UN-mediated armistice at Rhodes/Ras en-Naqoura/Mahanayim ending the 1948 war between Israel and Egypt (Iraq never signed).

name: Israel-Lebanon Armistice Agreement
summary: UN-mediated armistice at Rhodes/Ras en-Naqoura/Mahanayim ending the 1948 war between Israel and Lebanon (Iraq never signed).

name: Israel-Jordan Armistice Agreement
summary: UN-mediated armistice at Rhodes/Ras en-Naqoura/Mahanayim ending the 1948 war between Israel and Jordan (Iraq never signed).

name: Israel-Syria Armistice Agreement
summary: UN-mediated armistice at Rhodes/Ras en-Naqoura/Mahanayim ending the 1948 war between Israel and Syria (Iraq never signed).

name: War of Attrition ceasefire

violated.how: Egypt and the USSR moved surface-to-air missile batteries into the standstill zone immediately after the ceasefire, which the US confirmed.

summary: US (Rogers initiative) brokered ceasefire ending the War of Attrition.

name: Egyptian-Israeli Disengagement Agreement (Sinai I)
summary: Kissinger-brokered separation of forces on the Suez front after the Yom Kippur War.

name: Agreement on Disengagement between Israel and Syria

violated.how: The Golan line remained quiet for decades; Israel moved into the buffer zone after the fall of Assad in December 2024.

summary: Golan disengagement after the Yom Kippur War, creating the UNDOF buffer zone.

name: Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty

violated.how: Has held since 1979.

summary: Peace following the Camp David Accords; Israel returned Sinai, mutual recognition (US witness).

name: Algiers Agreement (1975)

violated.how: Saddam Hussein abrogated the agreement on 17 September 1980, days before invading Iran.

judgment.rationale: Historians generally treat Iraq's abrogation of the Algiers accord and claim to the Shatt al-Arab as a central casus belli of the Iran-Iraq War.

summary: Iran-Iraq agreement fixing the Shatt al-Arab border on the thalweg in exchange for Iran ending support for Iraqi Kurds.

name: Iran-Iraq ceasefire (UNSC Resolution 598)
summary: UN-monitored ceasefire accepted by both parties ending the Iran-Iraq War.

name: Safwan ceasefire talks
summary: Coalition-Iraqi military talks setting Gulf War ceasefire terms, formalised by UNSC Resolution 687 (3 April 1991).

name: Oslo I Accord
summary: Israel-PLO Declaration of Principles on interim self-government, witnessed by the US and Russia.

name: Israel-Jordan Peace Treaty

violated.how: Has held since 1994.

summary: Ended the state of war between Israel and Jordan (in force since 1948; last direct fighting in 1967) and fixed their border.

name: Abraham Accords
summary: Israel normalised relations with the UAE and Bahrain under US auspices; Morocco and Sudan followed, and Kazakhstan announced accession in November 2025.

name: 2024 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire agreement

violated.how: Israel kept forces at several positions in southern Lebanon after the withdrawal deadlines; the truce collapsed when Hezbollah (a non-signatory) attacked Israel on 2 March 2026.

summary: US/French-brokered cessation of hostilities after the Israel-Hezbollah war (Hezbollah approved but did not sign); broke down on 2 March 2026 when Hezbollah joined the Iran war.

name: Twelve-Day War ceasefire
summary: US-brokered (announced) ceasefire ending the June 2025 Israel-Iran war; no signed text. Superseded by the war that began 28 February 2026.

name: 2026 Iran war ceasefire

violated.how: Both sides violated it repeatedly and the US-Iran ceasefire collapsed on 8 July 2026 after attacks by both sides.

summary: Pakistan-mediated two-week ceasefire, extended indefinitely by Trump on 21 April; strained by blockades and the Lebanon front.

name: Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding

violated.how: The ceasefire collapsed on 8 July 2026 after attacks by both sides; US-side accounts cite Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

summary: US-Iran MoU signed by both presidents: halt to operations on all fronts, lifting of blockades, reopening of Hormuz and 60 days of nuclear talks.

name: 2026 Israel-Lebanon truce
summary: US-announced Israel-Lebanon truce during the 2026 Lebanon war (Israel vs Hezbollah), repeatedly extended; Hezbollah rejected later Israel-Lebanon frameworks.

name: Karachi Agreement
summary: UNCIP-supervised agreement delineating the Kashmir ceasefire line after the ceasefire of 1 January 1949.

name: Korean Armistice Agreement
summary: Signed by the UN Command (US), the Korean People's Army and the Chinese People's Volunteers; South Korea did not sign. No peace treaty followed.

name: Geneva Accords (1954)
summary: Cessation-of-hostilities agreements ending the First Indochina War and partitioning Vietnam at the 17th parallel pending 1956 elections (extra-state war, not in COW inter-state file).

name: International Agreement on the Neutrality of Laos

violated.how: North Vietnam kept about 7,000 troops in Laos and used the Ho Chi Minh Trail; the US later conducted a bombing campaign in Laos.

summary: Fourteen-nation Geneva agreement guaranteeing Laotian neutrality and the withdrawal of foreign troops.

name: Tashkent Declaration
summary: Soviet-mediated agreement restoring pre-war positions after the 1965 India-Pakistan war.

name: Simla Agreement

violated.how: Pakistani forces' 1999 Kargil incursion across the Line of Control contravened the commitment not to alter the LoC unilaterally.

summary: Post-1971 war agreement converting the Kashmir ceasefire line into the Line of Control and committing to bilateral settlement.

name: Paris Peace Accords

violated.how: North Vietnam's 1975 offensive conquered South Vietnam; both Vietnamese sides had violated the ceasefire from 1973.

summary: Ceasefire and US withdrawal agreement for Vietnam (PRG = South Vietnamese Provisional Revolutionary Government).

name: Lahore Declaration

violated.how: The Kargil infiltration in spring 1999, weeks after signing, contravened the declaration's commitments.

summary: India-Pakistan nuclear confidence-building and peace commitments signed by Vajpayee and Sharif.

name: Paris Peace Agreements (Cambodia)
summary: Comprehensive settlement of the Cambodian conflict following Vietnam's 1978-79 invasion, establishing UNTAC (principal signatories listed).

name: Sino-Vietnamese Land Border Treaty
summary: Land boundary treaty settling the border fought over in 1979 and 1984-87.

name: India-Pakistan ceasefire of 10 May 2025
summary: Ceasefire agreed between the two DGMOs after four days of strikes, announced first by President Trump.

name: Putrajaya ceasefire (Cambodia-Thailand)
summary: Malaysia-brokered unconditional ceasefire ending the July 2025 border war.

name: Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord

violated.how: Thailand suspended implementation on 10 November 2025 after a landmine injured Thai soldiers; full fighting resumed on 8 December 2025.

summary: Joint declaration consolidating the July ceasefire, signed by Hun Manet and Anutin, witnessed by Anwar Ibrahim and Donald Trump.

name: Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire of 27 December 2025
summary: Ceasefire signed by the two defence ministers at the border, reaffirming the July deal; reported holding as of mid-2026.

name: Doha ceasefire (Afghanistan-Pakistan)
summary: Qatar- and Turkey-mediated immediate ceasefire after the October 2025 clashes; collapsed in late February 2026 when open war began.

name: Rio de Janeiro Protocol

violated.how: Ecuador declared the protocol null in 1960 under President Velasco Ibarra, though the guarantors rejected this.

judgment.rationale: The incomplete demarcation of the Cordillera del Condor under the protocol is generally seen as the root of the 1981 Paquisha incident and the 1995 Cenepa War.

summary: Ended the 1941 Ecuadorian-Peruvian war, awarding most of the disputed Amazon area to Peru, with four guarantor states (the 1941 war is not in the COW inter-state file).

name: Treaty of Angra de Cintra
summary: Spain ceded the Tarfaya strip to Morocco, helping end the Ifni War.

name: Treaty of Guarantee (Cyprus)

violated.how: The Greek junta's July 1974 coup against Makarios sought union with Greece; Turkey invoked the treaty to invade, and its continued occupation is itself widely contested.

summary: Greece, Turkey and Britain guaranteed Cypriot independence and banned both union with another state and partition.

name: Geneva Declaration on Cyprus

violated.how: Turkey launched its second offensive on 14 August 1974 after the second Geneva conference broke down, until a ceasefire on 16 August.

summary: Tripartite (Turkey, Greece, UK guarantor) declaration consolidating the Cyprus ceasefire with a UNFICYP security zone; Cyprus itself (COW opponent in cow_184) not a signatory.

name: General Peace Treaty (El Salvador-Honduras)

violated.how: Implemented; the ICJ ruled on the border in 1992.

summary: Lima treaty formally ending the 1969 Football War and sending the border dispute to the ICJ.

name: Helsinki Final Act

violated.how: Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea is widely cited as a breach of the Act's principles of territorial integrity and inviolable frontiers.

summary: CSCE political commitments on the inviolability of frontiers, non-use of force and human rights (not a legally binding treaty).

name: INF Treaty

violated.how: The US formally found Russia in violation (9M729 missile) in 2014 and withdrew in August 2019; Russia denied the charge.

summary: Eliminated US and Soviet ground-launched missiles with 500-5,500 km range.

name: Chad-Libya ceasefire
summary: OAU-brokered ceasefire ending the Toyota War.

name: Framework Agreement on the Peaceful Settlement of the Territorial Dispute (Chad-Libya)

violated.how: Libya complied with the 1994 ICJ judgment.

summary: Algiers agreement referring the Aouzou Strip to the ICJ, which ruled for Chad in 1994; Libya withdrew by May 1994.

name: Ethiopia-Somalia peace agreement
summary: Agreement ending mutual support for rebel groups and disengaging forces after the Ogaden conflict (some sources date it 3 April 1988).

name: New York Accords (Tripartite Accord)
summary: Angola-Cuba-South Africa agreement: Cuban withdrawal from Angola and Namibian independence (ends the later South African Border War phase, not the COW 1975-76 war).

name: Madrid Joint Statement (Argentina-UK)
summary: Formal cessation of hostilities after the Falklands War under a sovereignty 'umbrella'; full diplomatic relations restored in February 1990.

name: Bishkek Protocol
summary: Russian/CIS-brokered protocol leading to the ceasefire of 12 May 1994 that froze the First Nagorno-Karabakh War; broke down in 2016 and 2020 amid mutual accusations.

name: Budapest Memorandum

violated.how: Russia annexed Crimea and backed the Donbas war in 2014, and invaded Ukraine in 2022.

summary: Security assurances to Ukraine (respect for its borders, no threat or use of force) in exchange for giving up Soviet nuclear weapons.

name: Itamaraty Peace Declaration
summary: Ceasefire and separation of forces ending the Cenepa War, with the Rio Protocol guarantors as witnesses.

name: Dayton Agreement

violated.how: The ceasefire and inter-entity boundary have held since 1995.

summary: Initialled at Dayton on 21 November and signed in Paris; ended the Bosnian War (witnessed by the US, UK, France, Germany, Russia and the EU).

name: Russian-Ukrainian Friendship Treaty

violated.how: Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea violated the treaty's mutual recognition of borders.

summary: Treaty of friendship, cooperation and partnership recognising the inviolability of existing borders; Ukraine let it lapse in 2019.

name: Brasilia Presidential Act

violated.how: Border demarcated and peace held since 1998.

summary: Definitive Peru-Ecuador peace and border settlement under guarantor arbitration.

name: Kumanovo Agreement
summary: Military-technical agreement between NATO/KFOR and Yugoslavia ending the Kosovo War with Yugoslav withdrawal from Kosovo.

name: Algiers Agreement (2000)

violated.how: Ethiopia refused to implement the 2002 Boundary Commission ruling awarding Badme to Eritrea until 2018.

summary: Comprehensive peace ending the Eritrean-Ethiopian War and creating a binding Boundary Commission.

name: Eritrea-Ethiopia Joint Declaration of Peace and Friendship
summary: Abiy-Isaias declaration formally ending the state of war; followed by the Jeddah agreement of 16 September 2018.

name: Six-point ceasefire plan (Russia-Georgia)

violated.how: Russia recognised Abkhazia and South Ossetia on 26 August 2008 and kept forces beyond pre-war positions, which the EU regarded as non-compliance.

summary: EU-mediated (French presidency) ceasefire; signed by Georgia 15 August and Russia 16 August 2008.

name: Djibouti-Eritrea Qatar-mediated agreement
summary: Qatar-mediated agreement to settle the Ras Doumeira border dispute, with Qatari peacekeepers deployed until 2017.

name: Sudan-South Sudan Cooperation Agreement
summary: Package of eight Addis Ababa agreements on security, oil and borders after the Heglig crisis (Abyei unresolved).

name: Minsk Protocol
summary: Trilateral Contact Group (OSCE, Ukraine, Russia) ceasefire for Donbas, also signed by DPR/LPR leaders; collapsed by January 2015.

name: Minsk II (Package of Measures)

violated.how: Russia recognised the DPR and LPR on 21 February 2022 and Putin declared the agreements no longer existed before the full invasion.

summary: Renewed Donbas ceasefire and political roadmap negotiated in the Normandy format (Germany, France).

name: Moscow ceasefire of 5 April 2016
summary: Ceasefire agreed in Moscow by Armenian and Azerbaijani chiefs of staff ending the Four-Day War.

name: Moscow Idlib ceasefire protocol
summary: Erdogan-Putin protocol (Russia acting for the Syrian government side) ending Operation Spring Shield, with joint patrols on the M4.

name: 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire agreement

violated.how: Azerbaijan's 2022-23 blockade of the Lachin corridor and its September 2023 offensive contravened the corridor and ceasefire provisions (Azerbaijan disputes this).

summary: Trilateral statement ending the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: territorial handovers to Azerbaijan and Russian peacekeepers on the Lachin corridor.

name: Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan peace protocol
summary: Agreement signed after the 16 September ceasefire failed, ending the September 2022 border war.

name: Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border treaty
summary: Japarov and Rahmon signed a treaty delimiting the entire border that had produced repeated armed clashes.

name: DRC-Rwanda Washington peace agreement

violated.how: Rwandan troops did not withdraw and M23 seized Uvira in December 2025; the US Treasury sanctioned the Rwandan military for violating the agreement in March 2026.

summary: Signed by the two foreign ministers under US auspices: Rwandan withdrawal, FDLR neutralisation, regional economic framework.

name: Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity

violated.how: The Rwanda-backed M23 offensive on Uvira (2-10 December 2025) followed within days; the US sanctioned the Rwandan military in March 2026.

summary: Signed by Presidents Tshisekedi and Kagame in Trump's presence, building on the June agreement; fighting continued days later.

name: Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement (Washington)
summary: Peace treaty text initialled (not signed) by Pashinyan and Aliyev at the White House, with a joint declaration mediated by Trump; formal signature and ratification pending.

name: US-Venezuela restoration of diplomatic relations
summary: After the January 2026 US operation that captured Maduro, the US and the Rodriguez-led government agreed to restore diplomatic and consular relations.

name: New START

violated.how: Russia suspended participation and inspections in February 2023, which the US State Department declared non-compliance.

summary: Strategic nuclear arms limits (1,550 deployed warheads) with verification; expired 5 February 2026 without replacement.
